title: Heavy-tier harness 4/5: one process-group stop (stop-group.js, sync variant for reap.js)
description:
Piece 4 of LIN-4219's approved plan: one way to stop a process group, used across the heavy tier. **Independent of pieces 1–3. No blockers.** It can run in parallel with piece 1. Its edits to `harbour.js` overlap piece 3's, so rebase on whichever lands first.

## Slice of the approved plan — implemented (pruned at close-out)

Implemented as approved in PR #317 ([https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/317](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/317>)), merged as `54febbf`: `stop-group.js` holds `stopGroup` / `stopGroupSync` / `groupAlive` / `KILL_GRACE_MS` (plus `recordGroup` / `forgetGroup` / `reapRecordedGroups`); Harbour is spawned detached and stopped as a group (stop and boot failure); `reap.js` uses `stopGroupSync`; a stranded group is reaped by the runner parent (`isolate-run.js`, `run-mutations.js`) from per-run records; the census is `test/harness-kill-census.test.js`. Deviations from the plan: the census allowlist dropped `e2e-smoke.js:1721` (a comment, which the census skips); `stopGroup`/`stopGroupSync` gained an optional `graceMs`. The full pre-prune plan text is preserved in the LIN-4223 task snapshots and the comment trail.

## Testing strategy (witnesses)

* Extend `test/system/harness-reap.test.js`. A leader spawns a grandchild. Stopping only the leader leaves the grandchild alive. Neither `stopGroup` nor `stopGroupSync` does. The file's two existing cases (normal exit and SIGTERM) keep passing.
* **Review note 2 witness:** a test file that ignores SIGTERM. After the runner's stop, no detached Harbour (or its group) survives.
* Manual check, recorded in the PR: Ctrl-C a single system file, then confirm no `node server.js` with PPID 1 remains.
* `npm test`, `npm run test:system` and `npm run test:mutation` are green.

## Acceptance

* Parent "Done when": **one way to stop a process group, used by the tier**, shown to leave no grandchild where a leader-only stop would.
* Parent "At merge: Gone": `stopGroup`/`groupAlive` in `run-mutations.js`, the leader-only kills, and ad hoc `kill(-pid)` outside the owner.
* **Likeliest break (plan):** group stop strands Harbour. The extended `harness-reap` cases and the SIGTERM-ignoring witness cover it.

---

**Parent:** LIN-4219 — *simple-dispatcher: the heavy test tier stands on one harness*. The parent's description holds the full scope, the "Done when" and "At merge" lists, the layout table and the **Implementation Plan**. Its comment trail holds the approving `### Plan Review Verdict` (comment `4ea51c1c-fa0a-44b9-9a63-c614f8fd7f56`). Read both before starting.

**Starting point:** the parent's approved plan is where this piece starts. Read it in full in LIN-4219's description, under "Implementation Plan". Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4219.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4219's approving plan-review (comment 4ea51c1c-fa0a-44b9-9a63-c614f8fd7f56, rev 1; the verdict names no revision number, and this is the only plan revision and the only verdict on the trail)
Grounding commit: simple-dispatcher `main` @ `502901c` (plan and review both grounded here; re-checked at breakdown on 2026-11-04, and nothing under `test/`, `docs/testing-and-ci.md`, `package.json` or `e2e-smoke.js` has changed)

**Constraints from the parent (all pieces):** nothing new at the repo root. `signal-guard.js` and `protected-paths.js` stay untouched. Each piece is its own PR, with its own run of `npm test`, plus `test:system` / `test:mutation` where the piece touches them. Out of scope, for the parent's close-out to list (not file): a scheduled/CI heavy-tier run (LIN-3160), pinned Harbour per dispatcher commit, splitting `run-mutations.js`, a test-infra module map, `e2e-smoke.js` joining the tier, the shared source sandbox.

comments.body:
**LIN-4223 · PR ready for review:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/317 (not merged)

**Commits** (branch `feat/lin-4223-stop-group`, head `75e5b039`): `cda8932` stop-group.js (beat 1) · `19ac0ec` harness wiring and reap witnesses (beat 2) · `75e5b03` census (beat 3).

**What changed:** one process-group stop for the heavy test tier. Harbour is spawned detached, and every Harbour and killer stop acts on the whole group through `test/system/harness/stop-group.js`. A stranded group is reaped by the runner parent from a per-run record. A census (`test/harness-kill-census.test.js`) bans hand-written group kills and leader-only stops in the tier.

**Tests on the final code (75e5b039):**
- `npm test`: 4027 run, 4022 pass, 5 skipped (already skipped on main), 0 fail.
- `npm run test:system`: 139 run, 137 pass, 2 fail. Both also fail on `main` (502901c) against the same LinearViewer checkout, so they are pre-existing and not from this PR: "a completed standalone run appears as a terminal session in the Sessions view" and "generating a run summary drives Harbour's real OpenRouter client to the fake (not the mock)".
- This PR's witnesses: stop-group 9/9, harness-reap 8/8, harbour-stop 5/5 (fake Harbour), census 4/4.

**CI:** `ci.yml`, check `unit tests` (Ubuntu, Node 22, `npm test`): **SUCCESS** on `75e5b039`.

**For the reviewer:**
1. `reapAll` is now SIGTERM, then a 5 s grace, then SIGKILL on the group, where it used to SIGKILL the leader at once. A tracked process that ignores SIGTERM can hold exit for about 7 s.
2. `test/isolate-run.js` gained a three-line runner-parent reap. It may conflict with LIN-4220; keep both sides if so.
3. `stopGroup` / `stopGroupSync` gained an optional `graceMs`. `recordGroup`, `forgetGroup` and `reapRecordedGroups` live in `stop-group.js`. The sync wait is zombie-aware.
4. The census lives at `test/harness-kill-census.test.js` and runs in the unit suite.
5. `run-mutations.js` imports only `stopGroup`.

**Left to LIN-4221:** the run-root side channel for `COULDNT_RUN` pre-flight reporting. This PR does not use or change it.

**Autopilot stepper run summary — LIN-4223 (implementation arc)**

Beats run in ONE warm session (ROOT dispatch aae14cab), each judged against the worker's evidence before advancing:
1. `cda8932` — `stop-group.js` extracted from `run-mutations.js`; sync variant is zombie-aware. 9 witnesses, 3 mutants caught (one only after the worker found and fixed a race in its own witness).
2. `19ac0ec` — Harbour spawned detached; boot-failure/stop() and `reapAll` go through group stop; stranded-group fallback (per-run pgid records, reaped by the runner parent in `test/isolate-run.js`). Fail-first output captured for reap, Harbour and fallback witnesses.
3. `75e5b03` — census `test/harness-kill-census.test.js` (rules a+b, reasoned allowlist, shrink-only check); cleanups routed through stop-group instead of allowlisted; two seeded violations caught with file:line.
4. Delivery — PR #317 (https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/317), head `75e5b039`.

**Verified by me (not just reported):** PR open/unmerged, 9 intended files only; CI check `unit tests` COMPLETED/SUCCESS on `75e5b039` (the only check in ci.yml); worker comment present on this ticket. Worker reports `npm test` 4027 run / 4022 pass / 5 pre-existing skips; `test:system` 137/139 with the same two failures on clean main (`observation-feed` terminal session, `tap1-openrouter` fake client).

**For review (flagged, not decided):** `reapAll` can now hold process exit up to ~7s on a SIGTERM-ignoring tracked process; `test/isolate-run.js` change may conflict with LIN-4220; the stranded-group fallback was placed in this piece (LIN-4221 owns the COULDNT_RUN side channel, untouched). Worker note: early in beat 1 it killed one pid it later realised it didn't own (a `node -e` child of a `node --test` process); it disclosed this and kept to its own pids afterwards.

**Left:** independent `review` → `close-out` (merge + Done). Not merged; LIN-4223 not Done.

## Review — LIN-4223

Reviewed PR #317 (https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/317), head `75e5b039a381c57e7d176eab2dceb88762f032db` (3 commits on `main` @ `502901c`). Nothing under `test/`, `e2e-smoke.js` or `package.json` has changed on main since the ticket was created, so the ticket still matches the code. No prior rulings on LIN-4223.

CI: green. `CI / unit tests` passed on `75e5b039` (Ubuntu, Node 22, `npm test` only). I also ran every suite myself on both branches (macOS, Node 25):
- `npm test`: PR 4027 run / 4022 pass / 0 fail / 5 skip; main 4023 / 4018 / 0 / 5. The +4 are the census tests.
- `npm run test:system`: PR 139 run / 137 pass; main 119 / 117. The **same two failures on both branches**, by name: "a completed standalone run appears as a terminal session in the Sessions view" and "generating a run summary drives Harbour's real OpenRouter client to the fake (not the mock)". This PR introduces no new failure.
- `npm run test:mutation` (PR): 67/67 killed, exit 0. The PR body did not report this run.

### Scope vs plan
The 9 files match the plan's slice: stop-group.js, harbour.js, reap.js, run-mutations.js, the census, the witnesses, plus a 3-line `isolate-run.js` reap. That `isolate-run.js` change is the "runner parent's cleanup" the plan's review note 2 named, so it is in scope. It does not conflict with PR #318 (LIN-4220): both PRs touch `isolate-run.js` and `run-mutations.js`, but GitHub reports #317 MERGEABLE, and whichever lands second rebases, as the ticket expects. The "Gone at merge" items are gone: `stopGroup`/`groupAlive`/`KILL_GRACE_MS` are no longer in run-mutations.js, and there are no leader-only kills in harbour.js/reap.js and no ad hoc `kill(-` outside stop-group.js. The ticket's allowlist entry `e2e-smoke.js:1721` was correctly dropped, because that line is a comment and the census skips comments. `run-system.js` `forward` is still a signal forward, so its allowlist entry is justified. `signal-guard.js` and `protected-paths.js` are untouched.

Regression check: LIN-4181 (which introduced reap.js) still holds. Its SIGINT/SIGTERM-exit witnesses pass. LIN-4196 (mutation runner edits only a copy) also holds: the record folder lives under the copy root, and the copy-root tests and the 67/67 run pass.

### Mutation checks (each reverted)
- reap.js `reapAll` put back to leader-only `child.kill('SIGKILL')` → 3 harness-reap group cases red ✔
- stopGroupSync made zombie-unaware (`groupAlive` instead of `groupLiveSync`) → "returns well inside the grace period" red ✔
- stopGroupSync with the SIGKILL escalation removed → the SIGTERM-ignoring cases never finish (the run hangs, not an assertion) ✔ caught, but the failure gives poor diagnostics
- harbour.js `stop()` made leader-only → 2 harbour-stop cases red ✔
- harbour.js boot-failure path: did not finish. That run was stopped while the mutant before it (`detached` removed) was hanging, so this mutant is not checked. Its witness stays in the ledger below.
- isolate-run.js runner-parent reap removed → "a test file SIGKILLed mid-run…" red ✔
- harbour.js `detached: true` removed → harbour-stop hangs ✔ caught (by hang)
- run-mutations.js `runIn`'s `reapRecordedGroups(groupRecords)`: **no test drives it**. No test starts a killer that starts Harbour (grep for `SD_HARBOUR_GROUPS`/`reapRecordedGroups` finds no witness outside harbour-stop's isolate-run case). See ledger item 1.

### Manual check (the ticket's Ctrl-C check, which the PR did not record)
I sent SIGINT to the process group of a single system file (`node --require ./test/isolate-run.js --test test/system/boot.test.js` on the PR) while its real Harbour was up (pid 99814, its own pgid). This is what a terminal Ctrl-C sends. Result: exit 130, Harbour gone, **0 `node server.js` with PPID 1**. Three other `node server.js` were running before and after; they belong to an unrelated parent (99640) and were left alone.

### Findings for close-out to fix
1. **Records left by the reaper path are never forgotten.** `reap.js reapAll` stops the group but does not call `forgetGroup`. So every Harbour that is reaped rather than `stop()`ped leaves its pgid in `<run root>/harbour-groups`. `isolate-run.js` then signals it again at the end of the run, which can hit a pgid the OS has since reused. This is exactly what harbour-stop's own assertion message says must not happen. Fix in `test/system/harness/harbour.js`, right after `recordGroup(...)`: `process.once('exit', () => forgetGroup(groupDir, child.pid));`. It is registered after `trackChild`'s exit handler, so it runs after `reapAll`. The SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers reach it too, through `process.exit`. It only needs to apply when `groupDir && child.pid`.
2. **Stale comment.** `test/system/mutation/run-mutations.js:27-28` says "only stopGroup is imported", but line 29 also imports `reapRecordedGroups`. Change it to: "The runner stops groups and reaps a killer's recorded Harbour groups; it does not read liveness itself, so groupAlive is not imported."

### What CI Did Not Prove
1. **inside** (review note 2, the stranded-Harbour fix, which names "stopGroup in run-mutations.js"): after a killer is stopped, `run-mutations.js` reaps the Harbour groups that killer recorded. This path has no witness; removing it turns nothing red. Settle **before the merge**: add a case to `test/mutation-runner.test.js`. A stub killer starts a detached group through `startHarbour` with a fake Harbour (like harbour-stop's FAKE_SERVER), ignores SIGTERM, and blocks until the runner's timeout stops it. Assert that the fake Harbour's leader and grandchild pids are gone after `runMutations` returns. Distinguishing precondition: the killer stays alive through the 5 s grace, so its own `reap.js` handler cannot stop Harbour and only `runIn`'s reap can. Check the case is red with `reapRecordedGroups(groupRecords)` removed from `runIn`.
2. **inside** (the sync variant): `stopGroupSync` reads liveness with `ps -A -o pgid=,stat=` for zombie-awareness. This has only been run on macOS. CI runs only `npm test`, and the stop-group/harness-reap/harbour-stop witnesses live in `test/system/`, which CI does not run. Settle **before the merge**: run `node --require ./test/isolate-run.js --test test/system/stop-group.test.js test/system/harness-reap.test.js test/system/harbour-stop.test.js` on a Linux host (e.g. the Ubuntu runner, or a container with Node 22). The distinguishing condition is "stopGroupSync … returns well inside the grace period" passing: a ps format that doesn't parse on Linux would fall back to signal liveness and sit out the 5 s.
3. **inside** (harbour.js boot-failure group stop): the mutation check for this path did not run (see above). Settle **before the merge**: in `harbour.js`, replace `stopGroupSync(child.pid, { graceMs: 0 })` with `child.kill('SIGKILL')`, confirm "a boot failure stops the Harbour group…" goes red, then revert.
4. **inside**, the limits of my own two-branch run: one macOS host, one run per branch (no flake separation), and it covers only `75e5b039`. Close-out re-checks CI on the exact commit it merges.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The deliverable is right and well witnessed: one group stop, used across the tier, with no grandchild left where a leader-only stop would leave one; the Ctrl-C check passes; system failures are the same as on main; 67/67 mutants killed. Close-out still has to make the two fixes above, add the run-mutations killer-reap witness (item 1), and run the Linux and boot-failure checks (items 2–3) before merging.

## Close-out — LIN-4223

**Merged:** PR #317 (https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/317), squash, pinned with `--match-head-commit ecddba6d65710cce5304a181db8c4bacc4c905d3`; merge commit `54febbf` on `main`. Authority: the recorded review Approve (comment `0ed4d754`), conditional on the ledger, settled below. The change is test-harness only (10 files under `test/`), so there is no deploy and no post-deploy step.

### Rebase (not a review item)
LIN-4220 (#318) landed on `main` while this was in review. Rebasing the three beats hit two conflicts in `test/system/mutation/run-mutations.js`: #318 had deleted `killerEnvFor`/`HARNESS_STATE_VARS` (replaced by `childEnv`), and this PR had deleted the old `stopGroup`/`groupAlive`. Resolved by keeping both deletions and building the killer env as `childEnv('run', { from: env, set: { HARBOUR_DIR, TMPDIR, SD_HARBOUR_GROUPS } })`, with the per-killer `reapRecordedGroups` kept. Also needed: #318's child-env census rejects a hand-built scrub of tracked names, so `harbour-stop.test.js`'s stand-in runner now uses `childEnv('run', { drop: ['SD_HARBOUR_GROUPS'] })` and its test file inherits the runner's env (commit `ecddba6`).

### Changes I made after the approval (each answers a review line)
| Commit (pre-squash) | Review line | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `87e7edf` | Finding 1 (records of reaped groups never forgotten) | `harbour.js`: `process.once('exit', () => forgetGroup(groupDir, child.pid))` right after `recordGroup`, registered after `trackChild`'s handler so it runs after `reapAll`. Witness added to `harbour-stop.test.js`: "a Harbour reaped at process exit, never stop()ped, leaves no record behind". |
| `87e7edf` | Finding 2 (stale comment) | `run-mutations.js:27-28` now says the runner stops groups and reaps a killer's recorded Harbour groups, and does not import `groupAlive`. |
| `87e7edf` | Ledger 1 (no witness for `runIn`'s reap) | New case in `test/mutation-runner.test.js`. |
| `ecddba6` | Consequence of the rebase onto #318 | See "Rebase" above (census rule, no behaviour change). |

### Ledger, settled
1. **`runIn`'s killer-group reap (inside): done, with the named precondition.** The stub killer starts a detached fake Harbour through the real `startHarbour`, removes reap.js's SIGTERM handler and ignores SIGTERM, then blocks until the runner's 4 s timeout; it is stopped only by the SIGKILL after the grace period, so its own handler cannot stop Harbour. First draft was **not** discriminating: the `finally` block's second `reapRecordedGroups` also cleaned up, so it passed with the line removed. The final case reads liveness at the moment the verdict is written (before the final reap). Mutant: `reapRecordedGroups(groupRecords)` removed from `runIn` → case RED ("the killer's Harbour leader survived the runner's stop of that killer"); restored → green. The `finally`-block reap has no separate witness; it is a backstop for an interrupt and was not on the ledger.
2. **`stopGroupSync` zombie-aware `ps` parsing on Linux (inside): done.** Ran `stop-group.test.js`, `harness-reap.test.js`, `harbour-stop.test.js` on GitHub's ubuntu-latest (Linux 7.0 azure, Node v22.23.4) from a throwaway branch (run 41831937179, branch deleted afterwards): 23/23 pass, including "kills the leader and its grandchild, and returns well inside the grace period" and both SIGKILL-escalation cases. The same 23 pass on macOS and on merged `main`.
3. **Boot-failure group stop (inside): done.** In `harbour.js`, `stopGroupSync(child.pid, { graceMs: 0 })` replaced with `child.kill('SIGKILL')` → "a boot failure stops the Harbour group, grandchild included…" RED ("grandchild … survived the boot-failure stop: only the leader was killed"); reverted. (The mutant leaves its fake grandchild running; I stopped it.)
4. **Limits of the review's own two-branch run (inside): re-checked on the final head.** CI on the exact merge commit, plus my runs below.
5. Review's note that the SIGKILL-escalation-removed mutant fails by hanging, not by assertion: accepted as is. It is caught, only with poor diagnostics. No ledger action asked, no change made.

No outside items on the review's ledger. No named monitor or rollback was recorded by review for this change; none is claimed.

### Evidence on the final head (`ecddba6`, local macOS, Node 25)
- `npm test`: 4128 run / 4123 pass / 0 fail / 5 skipped (the 5 skips are the same ones skipped on main).
- `npm run test:system`: 140 run / 138 pass / 2 fail. The two failures are the same two by name as on main and in the review: "a completed standalone run appears as a terminal session in the Sessions view" (LIN-4187) and "generating a run summary drives Harbour's real OpenRouter client to the fake (not the mock)" (LIN-4188). No new failure.
- `npm run test:mutation`: 67/67 killed, exit 0.
- Witnesses (stop-group, harness-reap, harbour-stop) 23/23; census tests (`harness-kill-census`, `child-env-census`) and `mutation-runner` 67/67 on merged `main`.
- The SIGKILLed-test-file witness still discriminates after the env change: removing the runner parent's reap in `isolate-run.js` turns it red.

### CI
- PR head `ecddba6`: `CI / unit tests` SUCCESS (run 41831925776). Merge was pinned to that commit.
- Merge commit `54febbf` on `main`: attempt 1 **failed**, attempt 2 passed. The failure was `test/state-store.test.js:50` "never loses a field under many interleaved concurrent writers" (`field f7 was lost`), in a file and module this PR does not touch (`git diff 52d2c3d 54febbf` over `test/state-store.test.js` and `state-store.js` is empty). Filed as an outside follow-up, LIN-4225. I am reporting it as a flake on the evidence of one failed and one passed attempt, not as proven.
- CI here runs only `npm test`; `test:system` and `test:mutation` are not in CI, so those results are from my own runs, not an author-independent environment.

### Not run
- The ticket's manual Ctrl-C check was not re-run by me. Review ran it on `75e5b039` (SIGINT to the group of a single system file: exit 130, Harbour gone, 0 `node server.js` with PPID 1). Rebase and the fixes did not change reap.js or the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers; the witnesses for that path pass.

### Related tickets and follow-ups
- Filed **LIN-4225** (flaky `state-store.test.js:50`; priority High, label Bug), related to LIN-459 and LIN-1663. Existing-ticket check: searched the tracker for the file and finding; no ticket names it. LIN-1663 and LIN-3159 cover flakes generally and are linked or noted, not duplicates.
- LIN-4224 (5/5) was blocked by this ticket; it is unblocked now (note posted there).
- Description archived (snapshot confirmed) and pruned: the discharged "Slice of the approved plan" section is replaced by a stub; the problem statement, testing strategy, acceptance, parent link and session-fit / plan-review lines are kept word for word.
